title: The Insane Story Behind John DeLorean

scenes.text: He was the youngest division head General Motors ever had. He walked away from it in nineteen seventy-three, built a stainless steel sports car in Northern Ireland, and was arrested in a Los Angeles hotel room on the nineteenth of October nineteen eighty-two. A jury later acquitted him on all eight charges. This is the story of John DeLorean, and every claim comes from a named source.
scenes.caption: THE INSANE STORY BEHIND JOHN DELOREAN

scenes.text: We used Wikipedia's pages on John DeLorean and on the DeLorean car, Encyclopedia dot com's account of the nineteen eighty-four trial, EBSCO's research starter, Ate Up With Motor, ThePricer and Business Insider. These sources disagree about numbers, dates and even a famous quote. We show those disagreements. Our own arithmetic is labelled.
scenes.caption: SOURCES: WIKIPEDIA · ENCYCLOPEDIA.COM · EBSCO · ATE UP WITH MOTOR · THEPRICER · BUSINESS INSIDER · SOURCES DISAGREE ON SEVERAL POINTS · OUR ARITHMETIC IS LABELLED

scenes.text: John Zachary DeLorean was born in Detroit on the sixth of January nineteen twenty-five, and died on the nineteenth of March two thousand five, at age eighty, from a stroke, Wikipedia says. He studied industrial engineering, then automotive engineering at the Chrysler Institute, and took an MBA at the University of Michigan in nineteen fifty-six.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: BORN 6 JAN 1925, DETROIT · DIED 19 MAR 2005, AGE 80 (STROKE) · B.S. LAWRENCE INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY 1948 · M.S. CHRYSLER INSTITUTE 1952 · MBA U. OF MICHIGAN 1956

scenes.text: His first big employer was Packard, where Wikipedia says he earned fourteen thousand dollars in nineteen fifty-three. In nineteen fifty-six he joined Pontiac at sixteen thousand dollars, as an assistant to Pete Estes and Semon Bunkie Knudsen. By our arithmetic, that is a fourteen percent raise in three years, and he was promoted to division chief engineer in nineteen sixty-one.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: PACKARD 1953, $14,000 · PONTIAC 1956, $16,000 (+14.3%, OUR ARITHMETIC) · CHIEF ENGINEER OF PONTIAC 1961

scenes.text: He is known for the Pontiac GTO, which began as a nineteen sixty-four option package, according to Wikipedia. In nineteen sixty-five, at age forty, he became Pontiac's division head, a record as GM's youngest. Wikipedia says the pace continued: on the fifteenth of February nineteen sixty-nine he was named head of Chevrolet, with a salary of two hundred thousand dollars.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: PONTIAC GTO — 1964 OPTION PACKAGE · 1965 PONTIAC DIVISION HEAD AT 40, GM'S YOUNGEST · 15 FEB 1969 HEAD OF CHEVROLET, SALARY $200,000

scenes.text: The Wikipedia page adds bonuses of up to four hundred thousand dollars. By our arithmetic, that makes his Chevrolet pay up to six hundred thousand a year, which is thirty-seven and a half times his sixteen thousand dollar Pontiac starting salary. Chevrolet's Vega reached three hundred ninety-five thousand, seven hundred ninety-two sales in the nineteen seventy-three model year.
scenes.caption: $200,000 + UP TO $400,000 BONUS = UP TO $600,000 vs $16,000 START = 37.5× (OUR ARITHMETIC) · WIKIPEDIA: VEGA 395,792 SALES IN MY1973 · CHEVROLET 1971 SALES >3 MILLION

scenes.text: In nineteen seventy-two he became GM vice president of car and truck production. He left GM on the second of April nineteen seventy-three, at age forty-eight by our arithmetic. Wikipedia says GM gave him a Florida Cadillac franchise as a retirement gift. His own verdict on his old employer, quoted there, was that they have too many bean counters and not enough engineers.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 1972 GM VP CAR AND TRUCK PRODUCTION · LEFT GM 2 APR 1973 (AGE 48, OUR ARITHMETIC) · GAVE HIM A FLORIDA CADILLAC FRANCHISE · QUOTE: 'THEY HAVE TOO MANY BEAN COUNTERS AND NOT ENOUGH ENGINEERS'

scenes.text: The sources disagree on when the company began. Wikipedia's DeLorean page says it was formed in nineteen seventy-three after he left GM, and the car page says the same. EBSCO says DMC was founded in Detroit in nineteen seventy-five. A third date in the car page is the Giugiaro contract, signed in March nineteen seventy-five. We report all three.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (JOHN + CAR PAGES): FORMED 1973 · EBSCO: FOUNDED IN DETROIT 1975 · GIUGIARO CONTRACT MARCH 1975 (WIKIPEDIA) → DATES CONFLICT; NOT RESOLVABLE FROM OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Wikipedia says he raised about two hundred million dollars, including four million of his own. By our arithmetic, his own money was two percent of the total. The rest came from investors and the British government. He was already connected: Wikipedia says he knew Johnny Carson, and that Lee Iacocca was best man at his second wedding.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: ~$200 MILLION RAISED, INCL. $4 MILLION OF HIS OWN = 2% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · JOHNNY CARSON INTRODUCED · LEE IACOCCA BEST MAN AT 2ND WEDDING

scenes.text: The factory was in Dunmurry, near Belfast. Wikipedia says the Northern Ireland Development Agency provided about a hundred million pounds in incentives, and the plant had more than two thousand workers at its peak. EBSCO adds that the British government invested to address high unemployment in Northern Ireland. So the cars were built partly with public money.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: ~£100 MILLION FROM THE NORTHERN IRELAND DEVELOPMENT AGENCY · 2,000+ WORKERS AT PEAK · EBSCO: BRITISH GOVERNMENT INVESTED TO ADDRESS HIGH UNEMPLOYMENT

scenes.text: The car itself took years. The DeLorean page says Giugiaro's contract was signed in March nineteen seventy-five, the first prototype appeared in October nineteen seventy-six, and the first production car was announced on the twenty-first of January nineteen eighty-one. By our arithmetic, that is about five years and nine months from contract to announcement.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: GIUGIARO CONTRACT MARCH 1975 · PROTOTYPE 1 OCT 1976 · FIRST PRODUCTION CAR ANNOUNCED 21 JAN 1981 → ~5 YR 10 MO FROM CONTRACT (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Along the way Lotus was brought in. Wikipedia says Colin Chapman re-engineered the car after a prototype went to Lotus in nineteen seventy-eight. The chassis became a steel backbone derived from the Lotus Esprit platform. Ate Up With Motor says the Lotus engineering work cost about twenty-three million dollars, billed directly to the DeLorean company in Britain.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: PROTOTYPE 2 TO LOTUS 1978; CHAPMAN RE-ENGINEERED; CHASSIS DERIVED FROM ESPRIT · ATE UP WITH MOTOR: LOTUS ENGINEERING ≈ $23 MILLION, BILLED TO DMC LTD.

scenes.text: The price promise slipped. The name DMC-12 came from a target of twelve thousand dollars, Wikipedia says, and the car launched at twenty-five thousand. The page also records a nineteen eighty-two price of twenty-nine thousand, eight hundred twenty-five. For the story of the man, the point is that the business plan and the product never lined up, as the sales later showed.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: '12' FROM A $12,000 TARGET · 1981 MSRP $25,000 · 1982 $29,825 · SALES LATER BELOW PLAN

scenes.text: Sales told the story. Wikipedia says that by the end of nineteen eighty-one about seventy-five hundred cars had been built and three thousand sold. October nineteen eighty-one was the best month, with seven hundred twenty sold, and January nineteen eighty-two only three hundred fifty. By our arithmetic, that is forty percent of production sold, and a fifty-one percent drop in three months.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: END-1981 ~7,500 BUILT, ~3,000 SOLD = 40% · OCT 1981: 720 · JAN 1982: 350 = −51% (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: John DeLorean's page puts it another way: by February nineteen eighty-two more than half of the roughly seven thousand cars produced were unsold, the company had about a hundred seventy-five million dollars of debt, and the factory went into receivership. In March, telegrams asked all three hundred forty-three dealers to buy six cars each, and none responded with an order.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (JOHN DELOREAN): FEB 1982 — >HALF OF ~7,000 CARS UNSOLD · ~$175 MILLION DEBT · RECEIVERSHIP · DMC-12 PAGE: MARCH 1982 TELEGRAMS TO 343 DEALERS ASKED THEM TO BUY 6 EACH · NO ORDERS

scenes.text: Money was moving too. Wikipedia says the British government found in January nineteen eighty-two that only eighty-five hundred cars had been built, and that twenty-three million pounds had been moved to a Panamanian account, money that never reached Lotus. It adds that Colin Chapman died at the start of the investigation.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (JOHN DELOREAN): JAN 1982 — BRITISH GOVERNMENT FOUND ONLY 8,500 CARS BUILT; £23 MILLION MOVED TO A PANAMANIAN ACCOUNT; NEVER REACHED LOTUS; CHAPMAN DIED AT START OF INVESTIGATION

scenes.text: Ate Up With Motor tells it differently. It says DeLorean transferred seventeen point six five million dollars to GPD Services, a Geneva-based holding company, five point one million of it from the British company and the rest from a US research partnership. It does not mention Panama. The two sources describe different accounts, in different currencies, and we cannot reconcile them.
scenes.caption: ATE UP WITH MOTOR: $17.65 MILLION TO GPD SERVICES (GENEVA) — $5.1 M FROM DMC LTD., REST FROM A US PARTNERSHIP · NO MENTION OF PANAMA · vs WIKIPEDIA: £23 M TO PANAMA → NOT RECONCILABLE (DIFFERENT AMOUNTS, CURRENCIES, PLACES)

scenes.text: Ate Up With Motor adds that a creditors' investigator, Malcolm Schade, reported about half the missing money ended up in a DeLorean personal account used to buy Logan Manufacturing in Utah, and the rest was never accounted for. It says Chapman died of a heart attack in December nineteen eighty-two, leaving prosecutors unable to disprove DeLorean's claim that the money was a personal loan from Chapman.
scenes.caption: ATE UP WITH MOTOR: INVESTIGATOR MALCOLM SCHADE — ~HALF OF MISSING GPD MONEY TO A DELOREAN PERSONAL ACCOUNT (BOUGHT LOGAN MANUFACTURING, UTAH) · CHAPMAN DIED DEC 1982 → CLAIM OF A PERSONAL LOAN COULD NOT BE DISPROVED

scenes.text: The factory was shut. Wikipedia says production stopped in May nineteen eighty-two. Ate Up With Motor says the British receivers shut down the British company in October nineteen eighty-two. The car page says Consolidated International later bought the unsold cars and assembled about a hundred more, with final production on the twenty-fourth of December nineteen eighty-two.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: PRODUCTION STOPPED MAY 1982 · ATE UP WITH MOTOR: BRITISH RECEIVERS SHUT DMC LTD. OCT 1982 · CONSOLIDATED INTERNATIONAL BUILT ~100 MORE · FINAL PRODUCTION 24 DEC 1982

scenes.text: Now the sting. Ate Up With Motor says James Hoffman, a federal informant with drug-trafficking convictions, approached DeLorean through a friend of his son. On the eleventh of July nineteen eighty-two they met at a hotel in Newport Beach, where Hoffman proposed a one point five million dollar brokerage fee plus three hundred thousand in expenses.
scenes.caption: ATE UP WITH MOTOR: JAMES HOFFMAN, FEDERAL INFORMANT WITH DRUG CONVICTIONS · 11 JULY 1982, NEWPORT BEACH MARRIOTT · $1.5 M BROKERAGE FEE + $300,000 EXPENSES · DELOREAN SAYS HOFFMAN MADE FIRST CONTACT

scenes.text: On the eighth of September, according to Encyclopedia dot com, FBI agent Benedict Tisa, posing as banker James Benedict, met DeLorean in San Carlos, California. On one tape the agent mentions an investor with profits from cocaine deals, and DeLorean replies that it looks like a good opportunity. The proposal was for DeLorean to invest one point eight million dollars.
scenes.caption: ENCYCLOPEDIA.COM: 8 SEPT 1982 — FBI AGENT BENEDICT TISA AS 'JAMES BENEDICT', SAN CARLOS, CA · TAPE: 'IT LOOKS LIKE A GOOD OPPORTUNITY' · PROPOSED INVESTMENT $1.8 MILLION · (ATE UP WITH MOTOR DATES A WASHINGTON MEETING 4 SEPT)

scenes.text: The sources disagree on what was bought. Encyclopedia dot com says thirty-four kilos of cocaine, expected to sell for five point one million dollars. Ate Up With Motor says one hundred kilos, two hundred twenty pounds. John DeLorean's Wikipedia page says a deal described as two hundred twenty pounds worth twenty-four million, while the FBI actually set up fifty-nine pounds worth six and a half million.
scenes.caption: ENCYCLOPEDIA.COM: 34 KG ≈ $5.1 M · ATE UP WITH MOTOR: 100 KG (220 LB) · WIKIPEDIA: DESCRIBED 220 LB (~$24 M); FBI SET UP 59 LB (27 KG, ~$6.5 M) · SOURCES CONFLICT

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, thirty-four kilos is seventy-five pounds, and fifty-nine pounds is twenty-seven kilos. So the sources give amounts of twenty-seven, thirty-four and a hundred kilos. They may describe the proposed deal, the amount at the hotel, and the headline figure differently. The pages do not explain, and the discrepancy is part of the case's confusing record.
scenes.caption: 34 KG = 75 LB · 59 LB = 26.8 KG · 220 LB = 99.8 KG (OUR CONVERSIONS) · WHICH FIGURE IS WHICH: NOT EXPLAINED IN THE SOURCES

scenes.text: Money was the motive, say the sources. Wikipedia says DeLorean's company was reportedly seeking seventeen million dollars to avoid insolvency. Encyclopedia dot com says he hoped to raise a fifteen million dollar loan through the San Carlos bank. EBSCO says he had been unable to secure more bank financing. Again the amounts differ, but all agree the company was running out of money.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: DMC SEEKING ~$17 M TO AVOID INSOLVENCY · ENCYCLOPEDIA.COM: HOPED TO RAISE A $15 M LOAN VIA THE SAN CARLOS BANK · EBSCO: COULD NOT SECURE MORE BANK FINANCING

scenes.text: The arrest came on the nineteenth of October nineteen eighty-two, in room five oh one of the Sheraton Plaza Hotel near Los Angeles airport, according to Ate Up With Motor. EBSCO says DeLorean saw the cocaine, remarked that it looked good as gold, and was arrested. Encyclopedia dot com says that on an earlier tape he described cocaine as better than gold.
scenes.caption: 19 OCT 1982, SHERATON PLAZA HOTEL, ROOM 501 (ATE UP WITH MOTOR) · EBSCO: 'GOOD AS GOLD' AT THE ARREST · ENCYCLOPEDIA.COM: TAPE 2 — 'BETTER THAN GOLD' (CORRECTION NOTE: NOT 'GOOD AS GOLD') → TWO QUOTES, TWO MOMENTS

scenes.text: Federal officials said they had more than a hundred hours of audio and video surveillance, Encyclopedia dot com says. He was held ten days in the Los Angeles County Jail, Ate Up With Motor says. On bail, the sources disagree by a factor of ten: EBSCO says two hundred fifty thousand dollars secured by property, Ate Up With Motor says a two and a half million dollar bond.
scenes.caption: ENCYCLOPEDIA.COM: >100 HOURS OF AUDIO/VIDEO · ATE UP WITH MOTOR: 10 DAYS IN LA COUNTY JAIL; $2.5 M BOND · EBSCO: $250,000 BAIL, SECURED BY HIS NEW YORK APARTMENT, NEW JERSEY ESTATE, PAUMA VALLEY HOME · 10× DISCREPANCY (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: He faced eight charges, EBSCO says. The newspaper reports of the arrest, the car page adds, came on the twentieth of October, and the company filed for bankruptcy on the twenty-sixth of October. By our arithmetic, that is seven days from arrest to bankruptcy filing, and the car page says the factory had already stopped in May.
scenes.caption: EBSCO: 8 CHARGES · WIKIPEDIA (CAR): ARREST REPORTS 20 OCT 1982; BANKRUPTCY FILED 26 OCT 1982 · 19 → 26 OCT = 7 DAYS (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The trial ran in Los Angeles, with Judge Robert Takasugi. Encyclopedia dot com gives the dates as the eighteenth of April to the sixteenth of August nineteen eighty-four, and Ate Up With Motor says sixty-two days of trial. The prosecutors were James Walsh and Robert Parry. The defence lawyers were Howard Weitzman and Donald Re. DeLorean did not testify.
scenes.caption: ENCYCLOPEDIA.COM: LOS ANGELES, JUDGE ROBERT TAKASUGI · 18 APR – 16 AUG 1984 · PROSECUTORS WALSH + PARRY · DEFENCE WEITZMAN + RE · ATE UP WITH MOTOR: 62 TRIAL DAYS · DELOREAN DID NOT TESTIFY

scenes.text: The defence was entrapment. Encyclopedia dot com says Weitzman argued DeLorean was vulnerable and desperate, and was coerced by government pressure. On cross-examination, agent Tisa admitted he had lied to a contact about receiving DeLorean's money, and had rewritten case notes and destroyed part of the originals. Ate Up With Motor says he admitted continuing the deal knowing DeLorean lacked the money.
scenes.caption: ENCYCLOPEDIA.COM: DEFENCE = VULNERABLE, DESPERATE, COERCED · TISA ADMITTED LYING TO A CONTACT, REWRITING NOTES, DESTROYING PART OF ORIGINALS · ATE UP WITH MOTOR: TISA CONTINUED THE DEAL KNOWING DELOREAN LACKED THE $1.8 M

scenes.text: The informant was damaged. Both sources say Hoffman admitted demanding a share of the seized money. Encyclopedia dot com says Judge Takasugi called him a hired gun and said the prosecution's late disclosure was offensive. Tapes showed Hoffman drinking heavily and making lewd remarks. By our arithmetic, the informant's credibility problems came from the government's own recordings.
scenes.caption: ENCYCLOPEDIA.COM + ATE UP WITH MOTOR: HOFFMAN SOUGHT A SHARE OF SEIZED MONEY · JUDGE TAKASUGI: 'HIRED GUN'; LATE DISCLOSURE 'OFFENSIVE' · TAPES: HOFFMAN DRINKING HEAVILY, LEWD REMARKS · 'FROM GOVERNMENT'S OWN RECORDINGS' = OUR READING

scenes.text: The closing arguments were theatrical. Prosecutor Walsh called DeLorean a man with the conscience of a tomcat. Weitzman compared the case to George Orwell's nineteen eighty-four, arguing the government rewrote history. Weitzman held daily press conferences outside the courthouse. Encyclopedia dot com adds that DeLorean told reporters afterwards, thank God for Howard.
scenes.caption: ENCYCLOPEDIA.COM: WALSH — 'A MAN WITH THE CONSCIENCE OF A TOMCAT' · WEITZMAN COMPARED THE CASE TO ORWELL'S '1984'; DAILY PRESS CONFERENCES · DELOREAN: 'THANK GOD FOR HOWARD' (REPORTEDLY)

scenes.text: The verdict came on the sixteenth of August nineteen eighty-four. Encyclopedia dot com says not guilty on all charges after twenty-nine hours of deliberation. EBSCO says all eight charges. Ate Up With Motor says the judge told jurors to acquit if they found entrapment, and they unanimously did. By our arithmetic, from the arrest to the verdict was twenty-two months.
scenes.caption: 16 AUG 1984 · NOT GUILTY ON ALL (8) CHARGES · 29 HOURS OF DELIBERATION (ENCYCLOPEDIA.COM) · UNANIMOUS ENTRAPMENT FINDING (ATE UP WITH MOTOR) · 19 OCT 1982 → 16 AUG 1984 ≈ 22 MONTHS (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Jurors said afterwards that they believed DeLorean had been entrapped and would not have engaged in criminal activity without the government's financial inducement, according to Encyclopedia dot com. That is a statement about the legal finding. It is not a finding that DeLorean was innocent of every wrongdoing, and the later fraud case, in the next chapter, shows the story was not over.
scenes.caption: ENCYCLOPEDIA.COM: JURORS — BELIEVED HE WAS ENTRAPPED; WOULD NOT HAVE ENGAGED IN CRIME WITHOUT GOVERNMENT INDUCEMENT · LEGAL FINDING ≠ FINDING OF OVERALL INNOCENCE (OUR NOTE)

scenes.text: The money case continued. Ate Up With Motor says that in nineteen eighty-five Detroit federal prosecutors charged DeLorean with fraud, tax evasion and racketeering, and that he was acquitted at an October nineteen eighty-six trial, about two months later. John DeLorean's page says a fraud and tax evasion indictment from nineteen eighty-five ended in an acquittal reported in December nineteen eighty-six.
scenes.caption: ATE UP WITH MOTOR: 1985 DETROIT CHARGES (FRAUD, TAX EVASION, RACKETEERING) → ACQUITTED ~2 MONTHS AFTER AN OCT 1986 TRIAL · WIKIPEDIA: 1985 INDICTMENT → ACQUITTAL REPORTED DEC 1986 (CONSISTENT)

scenes.text: In Britain, Ate Up With Motor says former Lotus managing director Fred Bushell was arrested in June nineteen eighty-nine and later pleaded guilty to fraud. The British crown also charged DeLorean, but his attorneys successfully resisted all extradition attempts. And it says Christina Ferrare filed for divorce after the nineteen eighty-four trial, seeking custody of their two children.
scenes.caption: ATE UP WITH MOTOR: FRED BUSHELL (EX-LOTUS MD) ARRESTED JUNE 1989, LATER PLEADED GUILTY TO FRAUD · BRITISH CROWN CHARGED DELOREAN — EXTRADITION RESISTED · CHRISTINA FERRARE FILED FOR DIVORCE AFTER THE 1984 TRIAL

scenes.text: EBSCO sums up the losses: the British government and investors, including Johnny Carson and Sammy Davis Junior, lost about two hundred fifty million dollars when the company failed. By our arithmetic, that is more than the two hundred million Wikipedia says DeLorean raised, so the two numbers measure different things. Neither source itemises them.
scenes.caption: EBSCO: UK GOVERNMENT + INVESTORS (INCL. JOHNNY CARSON, SAMMY DAVIS JR.) LOST ~$250 MILLION · WIKIPEDIA: ~$200 MILLION RAISED · 250 vs 200 = DIFFERENT MEASURES; NEITHER ITEMISED (OUR NOTE)

scenes.text: Later, his life became a series of attempts. Wikipedia says in nineteen ninety-four he filed a patent for a raised monorail, never built, sold watches online as DeLorean Time, and planned a new car called the DMC2. In nineteen ninety-nine he declared personal bankruptcy amid about forty legal cases, and in two thousand sold his four hundred thirty-four acre Bedminster estate, which Donald Trump later bought.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 1994 MONORAIL PATENT (NEVER BUILT), 'DELOREAN TIME' WATCHES, PLANNED DMC2 · 1999 PERSONAL BANKRUPTCY, ~40 LEGAL CASES · 2000 SOLD 434-ACRE BEDMINSTER ESTATE, LATER BOUGHT BY TRUMP

scenes.text: Wikipedia says he reportedly became a born-again Christian after the entrapment controversy, married four times, had three children, and in two thousand two married Sally Baldwin, with whom he had a daughter that year. His ashes are interred at White Chapel Cemetery in Troy, Michigan. The tombstone shows a DeLorean with its gull-wing doors open.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: REPORTEDLY BORN-AGAIN CHRISTIAN · MARRIED 4 TIMES · 2002 DAUGHTER WITH SALLY BALDWIN · ASHES AT WHITE CHAPEL CEMETERY, TROY, MI · TOMBSTONE SHOWS A DELOREAN WITH GULL-WING DOORS OPEN

scenes.text: Part of the story is the glamour. Wikipedia says he was a limited partner in the San Diego Chargers syndicate that bought a controlling interest for ten million dollars on the twenty-fifth of August nineteen sixty-six. He was one of fifteen investors in the New York Yankees, purchased from CBS for ten million on the third of January nineteen seventy-three.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: SAN DIEGO CHARGERS SYNDICATE, $10 M, 25 AUG 1966 (LIMITED PARTNER) · NEW YORK YANKEES — ONE OF 15 INVESTORS, $10 M FROM CBS, 3 JAN 1973
scenes.chapter: Before the sting: the celebrity years

scenes.text: Business Insider, in twenty nineteen, called John DeLorean the most flamboyant personality in the car business of his day, hands-on, on the celebrity circuit, including with Johnny Carson, who it says was a DeLorean owner and investor. That is a magazine's characterisation. The factual part is the investors' list, which Wikipedia and EBSCO both support.
scenes.caption: BUSINESS INSIDER (DEC 2019): 'MOST FLAMBOYANT PERSONALITY IN THE CAR BUSINESS OF HIS DAY' · CARSON = OWNER + INVESTOR (BI) · WIKIPEDIA + EBSCO: CARSON AMONG INVESTORS · CHARACTERISATION = OPINION

scenes.text: There is one more number from his personal history. Wikipedia says that during a period selling life insurance he sold about eight hundred fifty thousand dollars in policies in ten months. By our arithmetic, that is eighty-five thousand dollars a month. It is a small detail, but it fits the picture of a man who was good at selling, which is what the later company needed.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: ~$850,000 IN LIFE INSURANCE POLICIES IN TEN MONTHS → $85,000/MONTH (OUR ARITHMETIC) · 'WHAT THE COMPANY NEEDED' = OUR COMMENT

scenes.text: Put the dates on a line. Left GM in nineteen seventy-three. First prototype in nineteen seventy-six. First production car announced in January nineteen eighty-one. Factory production stopped in May nineteen eighty-two. Acquitted in August nineteen eighty-four. Died in two thousand five. By our arithmetic, the car was in production for under two years, from the announcement to the final cars in December nineteen eighty-two.
scenes.caption: 1973 LEFT GM · OCT 1976 PROTOTYPE · 21 JAN 1981 FIRST CAR ANNOUNCED · MAY 1982 FACTORY STOPPED · 24 DEC 1982 FINAL CARS · 16 AUG 1984 ACQUITTED · 2005 DIED · JAN 1981 → DEC 1982 ≈ 23 MONTHS (OUR ARITHMETIC; WIKIPEDIA)
scenes.chapter: The numbers of a short life

scenes.text: And the long tail. From the acquittal in nineteen eighty-four to his death in two thousand five is twenty-one years, by our arithmetic. In that time Wikipedia lists a patent, a watch brand, a planned car, a personal bankruptcy and the sale of an estate. From the day he left General Motors to the bankruptcy of his company was less than ten years.
scenes.caption: 16 AUG 1984 → 19 MAR 2005 ≈ 20.6 YEARS (OUR ARITHMETIC) · WIKIPEDIA: 1994 PATENT, WATCHES, DMC2 PLAN, 1999 PERSONAL BANKRUPTCY, 2000 ESTATE SALE · APR 1973 → OCT 1982 ≈ 9.5 YEARS (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The prototypes were sold off in the bankruptcy. The car page says Prototype One sold at the nineteen eighty-four auction for thirty-seven thousand dollars, and the Visioneering show car for twenty-one thousand, which United Press International put at fifty-eight thousand combined. By our arithmetic, those two cars sold for less than the price of three production DeLoreans at the nineteen eighty-three price of thirty-four thousand.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: PROTOTYPE 1 $37,000 + VISIONEERING CAR $21,000 = $58,000 (UPI) · 3 × $34,000 (1983 PRICE) = $102,000 > $58,000 (OUR ARITHMETIC; 1984 BANKRUPTCY SALES)

scenes.text: Compare with the cost of the show car. Wikipedia says Visioneering built the show car in nineteen seventy-nine at a cost of seven hundred fifty thousand dollars. It sold in the bankruptcy for twenty-one thousand. By our arithmetic, that is under three percent of its build cost. The whole story of the company, in miniature, is investment far above recovered value.
scenes.caption: $750,000 BUILD (1979) → $21,000 SALE (1984) = 2.8% (OUR ARITHMETIC; BANKRUPTCY SALE; NOT INFLATION-ADJUSTED) · 'COMPANY IN MINIATURE' = OUR COMMENT

scenes.text: The car lived on in the movies. Wikipedia and ThePricer both say the nineteen eighty-five film Back to the Future used the DMC-12, with six DeLoreans used in production plus a fibreglass one for flying scenes. John DeLorean's page lists two later screen portrayals: Lee Pace in the twenty eighteen film Driven, and Alec Baldwin in Framing John DeLorean, in twenty nineteen.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA + THEPRICER: BACK TO THE FUTURE (1985) USED THE DMC-12 · 6 CARS + 1 FIBREGLASS · JOHN DELOREAN PAGE: LEE PACE IN 'DRIVEN' (2018) · ALEC BALDWIN IN 'FRAMING JOHN DELOREAN' (2019)

scenes.text: The cars themselves became valuable. ThePricer says a standard DMC-12 now costs fifty to seventy-five thousand dollars, and a Part Three film car sold for five hundred forty-one thousand, two hundred dollars in two thousand eleven. By our arithmetic, the standard car's range is two to three times the twenty-five thousand dollar launch price, though not adjusted for inflation.
scenes.caption: THEPRICER: STANDARD $50,000–$75,000 (2026) · PART III CAR $541,200 (DEC 2011) · $50–75K ÷ $25,000 = 2–3× NOMINAL (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: And the brand itself. Wikipedia says a Texas company, founded in nineteen ninety-five by Stephen Wynne, now supplies parts and restoration, with no direct connection to the original firm. It lists legal disputes through twenty twenty-six, including an Italdesign judgment of four point six million dollars, and says its Alpha5 electric car had not launched as of August twenty twenty-six.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (DMC TEXAS): FOUNDED 1995 BY STEPHEN WYNNE · NO DIRECT CONNECTION TO ORIGINAL COMPANY · ITALDESIGN JUDGMENT $4.6 M (EARLY 2026) · ALPHA5 NOT LAUNCHED AS OF AUG 2026

scenes.text: Business Insider tied the story to Tesla in twenty nineteen, noting that Elon Musk was something of the John DeLorean of this era, though it argued he had far exceeded DeLorean's achievements. The Cybertruck is the first stainless steel vehicle produced since the DeLorean, Business Insider said in twenty twenty-four. These are the writers' comparisons, and we mark them as opinion.
scenes.caption: BUSINESS INSIDER (DEC 2019): MUSK 'SOMETHING OF THE JOHN DELOREAN OF THIS ERA' · BUSINESS INSIDER (MAR 2024): CYBERTRUCK = FIRST STAINLESS VEHICLE PRODUCED SINCE THE DELOREAN (OPINION / FACT AS LABELLED)

scenes.text: A list of disagreements. When the company was founded, nineteen seventy-three or seventy-five. Where the missing money went, Panama or Geneva. How much cocaine, twenty-seven kilos, thirty-four or a hundred. The bail, two hundred fifty thousand or two and a half million. And which gold quote was said when. We report each as found, because the record itself is inconsistent.
scenes.caption: FOUNDING 1973 (WIKIPEDIA) vs 1975 (EBSCO) · MONEY: PANAMA (WIKIPEDIA) vs GENEVA GPD SERVICES (ATE UP WITH MOTOR) · COCAINE 27 / 34 / 100 KG · BAIL $250,000 (EBSCO) vs $2.5 M BOND (ATE UP WITH MOTOR) · 'GOOD AS GOLD' vs 'BETTER THAN GOLD'
scenes.chapter: What the sources do not agree on

scenes.text: What our sources do not settle. Whether John DeLorean committed any crime in the Detroit and British matters. Where all of the missing money went. Who made the first approach in the sting, since Ate Up With Motor says DeLorean said Hoffman did. The courts acquitted him in the United States, and our sources do not say more than that. We do not offer a verdict of our own.
scenes.caption: UNSETTLED IN OUR SOURCES: FULL TRAIL OF THE MISSING MONEY · WHO MADE THE FIRST APPROACH (DELOREAN SAYS HOFFMAN) · BRITISH PROCEEDINGS' OUTCOME · COURT RESULTS: ACQUITTED 1984 (LA), ACQUITTED 1986 (DETROIT)

scenes.text: What is missing. The exact sum of the government's incentives in dollars. Why the jury and the judge saw the informant as they did beyond the trial record. Any statement by John DeLorean himself in a primary source that we read. If you know a primary document, tell us in the comments and we will update the description.
scenes.caption: NOT IN OUR SOURCES: GOVERNMENT INCENTIVES IN A SINGLE CONSISTENT CURRENCY · PRIMARY DOCUMENTS (COURT RECORDS, INTERVIEWS) · DELOREAN'S OWN ACCOUNT BEYOND THE QUOTES CITED
scenes.chapter: What our sources do not say

scenes.text: What do you think of the man who left the top of General Motors to build his own car and ended in a courtroom? Tell us in the comments.
